title: Domain Truncation in Parametric Elimination
originalTopic: Parametric Curves: Domain and Range Restrictions
author: Muhammad Abdullah Athar
problemStatement: Eliminate the parameter t from x = sqrt(t), y = 2t - 1 (t >= 0). Describe the resulting Cartesian curve, highlighting all domain constraints.
finalAnswer: y = 2x^2 - 1 \quad \text{for } x \ge 0; \quad \text{Right half of an upward-opening parabola}

steps.title: Solve for Parameter t
steps.explanation: Because x is the principal square root of t (where t >= 0), x cannot take negative values: x in [0, inf).
steps.why: The range of the principal square root function is [0, inf), imposing a strict domain restriction on x.

steps.title: Substitute into the y-Equation
steps.explanation: Substituting t = x^2 yields the quadratic equation y = 2x^2 - 1.
steps.why: Algebraic substitution yields the governing Cartesian relation.

steps.title: State the Restricted Cartesian Curve
steps.explanation: The graph is not the full parabola; it is only the right branch beginning at vertex (0, -1) and extending upward and to the right.
steps.why: Parameter restrictions must be faithfully transferred to the Cartesian domain to prevent geometric distortion.
